text:
Sam: heads-up — running into weirdness with header-driven model selection when customers send model metadata in X-Model-Metadata. Some manifests include capabilities like `quantized=true` and `kv_cache=false` and our current matcher just does substring matches.
Maya: can you paste an example?
Sam: sure:
Sam: ```json
{
  \"model_alias\": \"text-compact-1\",
  \"metadata\": {\"quantized\": \"true\", \"kv_cache\": \"false\"}
}
```
Sam: customer sends header `X-Model-Metadata: quantized=true;kv_cache=false` and it matches text-compact-1 and falls back to text-compact-1-v2 which lacks kv cache -> incorrect because fallback loses kv_cache capability.
Julien: ugh. that's the compatibility hole we've talked about. Current routing only checks alias string equality or simple header contains. We need predicate logic (AND/OR/not) and explicit capability checks.
Maya: do we want to extend header grammar or normalize into request attributes in the gateway? I vote normalize (split into map) then evaluate rules against structured fields.
Liam: normalization SGTM. We should also surface a compatibility mismatch metric so Console can flag when a chosen fallback differs on a capability.
Ana: for UX: show chosen model + reason and a small change indicator (e.g., loses: kv_cache) so users see regression immediately.
Sam: agreed. Also need a server-side safety: if fallback changes a required capability (explicitly requested by header) we should reject or fall back to a compatible variant in a different family, not blindly pick next alias.
Maya: example rule idea: `if header.requested.kv_cache == true and candidate.metadata.kv_cache != true then skipCandidate`
Julien: or add compatibility expressions to routing rules: `requires: [kv_cache, half_precision]` and `compatibility: STRICT|BEST_EFFORT`. BEST_EFFORT could allow degraded capability with telemetry.
Liam: telemetry: emit `route.compatibility_score` and `route.capability_delta` as tags. That lets Optimize recommend quantization profiles per workload.
Sam: code sketch for normalized matcher:
Sam: ```javascript
// gateway middleware
const attrs = parseMetadataHeader(req.headers['x-model-metadata']); // -> {kv_cache: true, quantized: true}
const candidates = resolveAliases(route.match);
const pick = candidates.find(c => matchesRequired(c.metadata, attrs.required));
if (!pick && route.compatibility === 'BEST_EFFORT') pick = bestEffort(candidates, attrs);
// otherwise return 409 with explanation
```
Maya: we should return a structured 409 body with `requested_capabilities` and `closest_candidate` plus `diff` so SDKs can surface it.
Ana: console: add a compact warning icon next to rollout entries when compat deltas > 0. Also allow override toggles per-route (force-best-effort) with audit log.
Julien: question: how does this interact with quotas? If a strict-compatible model is in Dedicated pool with limited quota, but best-effort fallback is hosted and cheaper, apps might prefer fallback. We need policy: `prefer_compatibility_over_cost` flag or weight knobs.
Liam: yes — route policy should be multi-dimensional: capability_priority, cost_priority, latency_priority. Score candidates and pick top. Record decision trace.
Sam: rollout-bot: started canary deployment for route /v1/generate with compatibility_policy=STRICT at 2026-03-18 15:05:00.
rollout-bot: deployment-id=canary-2026-03-18-15:05, targets=5% traffic, note=compatibility-strict.
Maya: can we add a dry-run mode that logs alternative picks without impacting traffic? helpful for customers to preview compat impact.
Julien: yes — gateway can compute `alt_pick` and include `X-Alternate-Picks` header for debugging or `X-Alt-Picks-Blob` S3 link if big.
Ana: follow-ups: 1) spec for normalized header -> api@docs, 2) console UX mock for capability deltas (I'll take), 3) telemetry schema for compatibility_score (Liam), 4) gating behavior for STRICT vs BEST_EFFORT (Julien).
Sam: assigning: Maya will draft header normalization PR, Julien draft routing policy extension, Liam telemetry schema, Ana console mocks. I'll prototype the gateway matcher.
Maya: ETA for PRs? 2w for normalization, 1w for draft policy doc.
Julien: I'll get compatibility gating doc in 5 days.
Liam: telemetry schema in 3 days, will include tag examples and prometheus + tracing mappings.
Ana: console mocks in 7 days.
Sam: thanks. One more: add unit tests that assert fallback never changes a `required` capability. Write tests in eng-platform infra repo.
Liam: noted — will add CI check that flags any route config that enables BEST_EFFORT for routes with `requires` set.
Sam: cool. I'll open a single epic in Jira linking all PRs.
Maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
